prompt:
Build a battery-fed electric axle-drive model in Simulink for a 1100 kg vehicle. The physical power path must include a high-voltage DC source, DC link, controlled three-phase converter, interior permanent-magnet synchronous motor, fixed 9:1 gear reduction, differential/axle load, wheels, and finite-mass longitudinal vehicle dynamics. The motor must operate in both motoring and generating modes. A connected drive controller must convert the driver's accelerator and brake requests into a bounded torque reference and regulate the motor through measured phase currents and rotor/electrical state. Acceleration and regenerative braking torque must act through the converter, motor, gear, and vehicle path; prescribed vehicle speed or replayed torque/current trajectories are not valid.

Read ev_drive_input from the MATLAB base workspace. acceleration_scale is in 0.45--1.00 and brake_scale is in 0.40--1.00. Multiply the published 0--5 s accelerator and brake base profiles by these scales and clip pedal values to [0,1]. Use the published incline and zero-wind profiles unchanged. Use the fixed public vehicle and drive constants. The exact current-controller realization, coordinate transforms, switching abstraction, and torque-control equations are not prescribed, but the electrical feedback path and electromechanical/vehicle energy path must be causal and connected. Changing acceleration_scale or brake_scale must materially change torque, current, and vehicle response.

Log complete-run MATLAB Timeseries named driver_input, motor_torque, phase_currents, and vehicle_speed. driver_input has width 2 in this order: applied accelerator and brake, both unitless fractions. motor_torque has width 4 in this order: controller torque reference, actual shaft torque, controller-estimated torque, and symmetric torque limit, all in N*m. phase_currents has width 3 in this order: phase-a, phase-b, and phase-c current, all in A. vehicle_speed has width 1: vehicle speed in km/h. motor_torque must contain the controller reference, actual shaft torque, controller-estimated torque, and symmetric torque limit. phase_currents must be the actual three-phase currents in the motor drive. vehicle_speed must come from the finite-mass vehicle state. driver_input must contain the applied, clipped accelerator and brake profiles. All logs must arise from the same simulation. The model should track achievable torque, remain finite under every declared scale pair, accelerate under positive demand, enter generating torque under braking, and show a physically consistent change in final speed when braking is reduced. Save the completed model as cand_XAUTO07.slx in the submission directory and keep the latest usable state saved there throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XAUTO07.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
